instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company connects its data center to one VPC with two Site-to-Site VPN connections to a virtual private gateway. The connections use static routing. Nightly transfers now need several times the bandwidth of one VPN tunnel, and the design must be scalable as the transfers grow. The company does not want to use AWS Direct Connect yet. The customer gateway devices support BGP. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Use dynamic routing with BGP for the VPN connections, and advertise the data center prefixes from the customer gateway devices on every tunnel.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach the VPN connections to a transit gateway instead of the virtual private gateway, and turn on equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing support on it.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on acceleration for the existing VPN connections, so that the tunnels use the AWS global network and carry more traffic each night.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the virtual private gateway with software VPN appliances on Amazon EC2 instances, and split the tunnels across the instances with custom routing scripts.

options.label: E
options.text: Add three more Site-to-Site VPN connections to the existing virtual private gateway, and spread the data center prefixes across all of the tunnels.

items.stem: A company runs a mission-critical application in AWS that reads order data from its on-premises data center every minute. The data center connects to AWS through one AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection at one Direct Connect location. The connectivity must survive the failure of a device, a connection, or a whole Direct Connect location. Which design will make the connectivity the MOST resilient?

options.label: A
options.text: Add connections at a second Direct Connect location, so that each of the two locations has two connections that end on separate devices.

options.label: B
options.text: Add three dedicated connections at the current location, and combine all four connections in a link aggregation group (LAG) for the traffic.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a second dedicated connection at the current location, and make sure that it ends on a different AWS device from the first one.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the current dedicated connection, and add a Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet as the backup path for the traffic.

items.stem: A company has one AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection at a location in the United States. A private virtual interface on the connection is attached to the virtual private gateway of a VPC in us-east-1. The company adds a VPC in eu-west-1, a second Region, and that VPC must reach the data center privately over the same connection. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Direct Connect gateway, attach a new private virtual interface to it, and associate the virtual private gateways of both VPCs with it.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a transit gateway in each Region, attach each VPC to the transit gateway in its Region, and connect both through a transit virtual interface.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a public virtual interface on the connection, and use it to reach the private IP addresses of the VPC in eu-west-1.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a second private virtual interface on the connection, and attach it directly to the virtual private gateway of the VPC in eu-west-1.

items.stem: A company has employees who work from home on laptops. The employees must reach internal applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets of a VPC in one AWS Region. They must sign in with the company's existing SAML 2.0 identity provider. The company wants a fully managed remote access solution. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection from each laptop to a virtual private gateway, with one customer gateway for each employee.

options.label: B
options.text: Order an AWS Direct Connect hosted connection for each home office, and attach a private virtual interface to the VPC for each one.

options.label: C
options.text: Run an OpenVPN server on an Amazon EC2 instance, connect it to the identity provider, and patch and scale the instance as users grow.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an AWS Client VPN endpoint that uses federated authentication with the SAML 2.0 identity provider, and give users the AWS provided client.

items.stem: A company uses a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection as the primary path from its data center to a virtual private gateway. A Site-to-Site VPN connection to the same virtual private gateway is the backup path for this mission-critical traffic. However, in a failover test, the VPN cannot carry the load. The company needs a highly available design in which the backup path carries the full load when the primary connection fails. Which solution will provide the HIGHEST availability?

options.label: A
options.text: Order a second 10 Gbps Direct Connect connection at a second Direct Connect location, and use it as the backup path for the traffic.

options.label: B
options.text: Add three more Site-to-Site VPN connections to the same virtual private gateway, so that the backup tunnels can share the full load.

options.label: C
options.text: Use AS path prepending on the Direct Connect routes, so that the VPN connection carries part of the traffic at all times.

options.label: D
options.text: Order a second 10 Gbps connection at the same Direct Connect location, and add both connections to one link aggregation group (LAG).

items.stem: A company has a Site-to-Site VPN connection between its data center and a virtual private gateway. The customer gateway device has only one of the two tunnels configured, and it uses static routing. During an AWS tunnel endpoint update, connectivity to the VPC stopped for several minutes. The company needs the VPN to be highly available, with minimal downtime during future updates. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a second VPN connection to the same virtual private gateway from a new customer gateway device, and configure one tunnel on each device.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on tunnel endpoint lifecycle control for the connection, and schedule each AWS update for a time when the single tunnel is not busy.

options.label: C
options.text: Attach a second virtual private gateway to the VPC, and create a second VPN connection with one tunnel that ends on the new gateway.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure the second tunnel of the existing VPN connection on the customer gateway device, so that traffic can move to it during an update.

items.stem: A company must connect its on-premises data center to a VPC in one AWS Region. All traffic between the data center and the VPC must be encrypted in transit. The connection must be ready as soon as possible, within one week, and the traffic is low. The company has a router in the data center that supports IPsec. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Launch a software VPN appliance on an Amazon EC2 instance in the VPC, and connect it to the data center router with IPsec over the internet.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet from the data center router to a virtual private gateway that is attached to the VPC.

options.label: C
options.text: Order a new AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection, and launch a software VPN appliance on an Amazon EC2 instance that ends IPsec over the connection.

options.label: D
options.text: Order a new AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection, and create a Site-to-Site VPN connection over it from the data center router to the VPC.

items.stem: A company sends traffic from its data center to a VPC over a private line: an AWS Direct Connect connection with a private virtual interface. A new security rule says that all traffic on this connection must be encrypted in transit. The connection is a 1 Gbps hosted connection from a Direct Connect Partner. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on TLS encryption in every application that sends data between the data center and the VPC, and keep the virtual interface unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on MACsec for the Direct Connect connection, and configure the matching MACsec keys on the company router at the Direct Connect location.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection that runs IPsec over the Direct Connect connection, and route the VPC traffic through the VPN tunnels.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the current design, because traffic on a Direct Connect connection stays off the internet and is encrypted on the private line.

items.stem: A company runs an analytics workload in a VPC. The company needs a private line from its data center to the VPC that does not use the internet. A capacity of 200 Mbps is sufficient for the next three years. The company has no network equipment in a Direct Connect location and does not want to place any there. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet to a virtual private gateway, and size the customer gateway device for 200 Mbps.

options.label: B
options.text: Request a 10 Gbps dedicated connection, and work with a partner to extend the data center network to the Direct Connect location.

options.label: C
options.text: Request a 200 Mbps dedicated connection in the Direct Connect console, and order a cross-connect at the Direct Connect location.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask an AWS Direct Connect Partner for a 200 Mbps hosted connection, and create a private virtual interface on it to the VPC.

items.stem: A company has an AWS Client VPN endpoint that is associated with a subnet of a VPC, and remote users reach resources in that VPC. The VPC reaches an on-premises network, 172.16.0.0/16, through a Site-to-Site VPN connection, and its route tables and security groups already allow traffic from the client CIDR range. Users must also reach the on-premises network through Client VPN. The company wants to restrict the tunnel to traffic for the VPC and the on-premises network. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Change the client CIDR range of the endpoint to 172.16.0.0/22, so that clients get addresses inside the on-premises network range.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a new Client VPN endpoint with split-tunnel turned on, copy the routes and rules to it, and move every user to the new endpoint.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on split-tunnel on the existing endpoint, so that only traffic that matches a route in the endpoint route table uses the tunnel.

options.label: D
options.text: Add an authorization rule that denies access to 0.0.0.0/0, so that internet traffic from the clients cannot use the tunnel.

options.label: E
options.text: Add a route to 172.16.0.0/16 through the associated subnet in the endpoint route table, and add an authorization rule for 172.16.0.0/16.

items.stem: A company must connect its on-premises data center to a VPC in one AWS Region. All traffic between the data center and the VPC must be encrypted in transit. The company needs consistent network performance for large, steady transfers, and the connection can be ready in four months. The company has a router in the data center that supports IPsec. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Order a new AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection, and launch a software VPN appliance on an Amazon EC2 instance that ends IPsec over the connection.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet from the data center router to a virtual private gateway that is attached to the VPC.

options.label: C
options.text: Launch a software VPN appliance on an Amazon EC2 instance in the VPC, and connect it to the data center router with IPsec over the internet.

options.label: D
options.text: Order a new AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection, and create a Site-to-Site VPN connection over it from the data center router to the VPC.

items.stem: A company sends traffic from its data center to a VPC over a private line: an AWS Direct Connect connection with a private virtual interface. A new security rule says that all traffic on this connection must be encrypted in transit. The connection is a 10 Gbps dedicated connection, the router and location support MACsec, and the encryption must not reduce the MTU. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection that runs IPsec over the Direct Connect connection, and route the VPC traffic through the VPN tunnels.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on MACsec for the Direct Connect connection, and configure the matching MACsec keys on the company router at the Direct Connect location.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on TLS encryption in every application that sends data between the data center and the VPC, and keep the virtual interface unchanged.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the current design, because traffic on a Direct Connect connection stays off the internet and is encrypted on the private line.
